s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive hip pain with night pain and weight loss, associated with limited range of motion and synovitis
salient_findings: Progressive left hip pain radiating to the anterior thigh
Reduced range of motion of the left hip with spasms and tenderness
Synovitis and marrow edema on MRI
key_facts: 1-year history of progressive left hip pain
Pain radiates to the anterior thigh
Pain is severe at night
Associated with weight loss and anorexia
No history of trauma
Antalgic gait
Reduced range of motion of the left hip in all planes
Tenderness deep in the left groin
Normal laboratory studies, including complete blood count, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and C-reactive protein
Unremarkable pelvic radiograph
MRI shows synovitis and marrow edema without fracture
No clinical improvement with empirical anti-tubercular therapy
Open synovial biopsy shows mild to moderate chronic synovitis with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates
Negative cultures and unremarkable rheumatologic evaluation

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma

shortlist.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive hip pain, weight loss, and anorexia, with chronic synovitis and marrow edema

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of progressive hip pain, radiating to the anterior thigh, severe at night, and associated with weight loss and anorexia, along with the MRI findings of a well-defined lesion with a thick sclerotic rim and associated marrow edema, is consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis, which can cause bone lesions and systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: Chronic osteomyelitis
rejected.why: Normal laboratory studies, including complete blood count, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and C-reactive protein, make chronic osteomyelitis less likely

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: The patient's age and the lack of a clear mass on imaging make Ewing's sarcoma less likely

rejected.label: Osteosarcoma
rejected.why: The absence of a clear aggressive bone lesion on imaging and the lack of elevated laboratory markers make osteosarcoma less likely

rejected.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
rejected.why: The patient's systemic symptoms, such as weight loss and anorexia, and the presence of a well-defined bone lesion are not typical of pigmented villonodular synovitis
